notes.title: Expeditions Update | Available now
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/971d7991c893a7c5d556dfae51fd9d0ebecfab6e.gif[/img]

[b]Greetings, survivors![/b]

[i]Exactly 2 weeks ago, Endzone - A World Apart launched into Early Access. Many players of the Closed Beta Phase were visibly confused why expeditions were suddenly no longer available. We used the time to continue to work on the expeditions and to expand them. Today is the day when all players can finally access and use the new system to explore the world of Endzone - A World Apart. So with this update, the big content update from April is released and we tick off the first item on our Roadmap. Please note, however, that the expedition system also falls under Early Access and will be expanded and optimized by future updates.[/i]

[h3][b]Important: Older Savegames are not compatible with this version.[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/358f4e218820d14ba28920be33e1bc1eab7201e5.gif[/img]

[list]
[*]Added the [b]Expedition Station[/b] building. This is the central hub to start new and manage ongoing expeditions on the map.
[*]Added an Expedition Window to assemble your expedition crew carefully. Add experienced professionals, give them tools, protective clothing or special resources that can help them to fulfill their tasks.
[*]Added scouts. [b]Scouts[/b] are a new profession, they unlock new locations on your map to send expeditions to, while also helping to set up your expedition with expedition rations.
[*]Experience 12 unique stories with different branches and a complex decision making system. Guide your expedition through old buildings and relics of the old world.
[*]New Soundtrack for the Expeditions.
[*]Added a preloading system to avoid system hangs and freezes. This will show up as a loading bar right after the intro video.
[*]Added explanation for settler badges to explain how settlers can earn badges.
[*]Added a popup to show our Roadmap at the start of the game (can be disabled).
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/eeaf459ebeb01edf2f143de20507ffaba9b2d2a0.gif[/img]
[list]
[*]Reworked the upgrade system. Buildings are not disassembled before an upgrade anymore. They will stay intact while visually upgrading to their new form.
[*]Market: Now iterates over all chosen resources.
[*]Market: No longer stocks resources that are not in the selected resources list.
[*]Market: Now correctly uses the area of influence to gather resources.
[*][b]Irrigation Plant[/b]: When loading a [b]Savegame[/b], the [b]Irrigation Plant[/b] now correctly remembers its last irrigation setting
[*]Camera no longer rotates while being in the Main Menu as this was causing nausea for some players.
[*]Game Speed is now only reset to default or paused when leaving the Main Menu.
[*]Fixed pivot points of barrels and [b]Power Poles[/b]
[*]The [b]Irrigation Plant[/b] now slowly changes the radiation level of the environment according to the radiation level of the water in its inventory.
[*]Fixed wrong linkage to several glossary headlines when clicking on the “?” symbol in the inspector.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/9b45befc9d99249c0c5d7ab04bd584eb3146e462.gif[/img]
[list]
[*]The player now starts with 2 random field seeds and 1 random plantation seed. The other seeds are locked at the start as Expeditions are now part of the game and the player has to search for new seeds.
[*][b]Market[/b]: Now accepts Wood & Scrap
[*][i]Pathfinding[/i]: Improved performance
[*][i]TaskService[/i]: Improved performance
[*][i]DrawbackService[/i]: Improved performance
[*]Map Generation: Changed ruin distribution amounts so the scenery doesn’t look as repetitive as before while also changing the amount of spawned story ruins.
[*]Decreased building costs of the [b]Shelter[/b]. ([b]Wood[/b]: [i]96 -> 68[/i], [b]Scrap[/b] [i]180 -> 100[/i], [b]Plastic[/b] [i]12 -> 6[/i], [b]Cloth[/b] [i]10[/i], [b]Building Time[/b] [i]300 -> 250[/i])
[*][b]Irrigation Plant[/b]: Increased the [b]Area of Influence[/b] from ([i]26 -> 36[/i])
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/ec24c6b5efe3d99ce3ed2c8ca69509be7727a983.gif[/img]
[list]
[*]The [b]Forester Lodge[/b] and its work mode: “Cut & Reforest” is currently unbalanced. Trees are cut down faster than the time it takes to replant and regrow them.
[*]Settlers currently do not get the protection clothing with the best protection value but simply the one that is the closest.
[*]Using the loot and return window to get the collected resources from an expedition back has some issues, when filling up the capacity.
[*][h3][b]Older Savegames are not compatible with this version.[/b][/h3]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/4baf720351646c58f0535e53e3ab5976dbf39a8e.gif[/img]

To be able to send out expeditions, an [b]Expedition Station[/b] must first be built. In this building [b]Scouts[/b] can be assigned as workers. An [b]Expedition Station[/b] requires [b]36[/b] wood, [b]58[/b] scrap, [b]16[/b] metal and [b]18[/b] plastic to build.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/9a22d4f039ecbb4de7f1e6f5d5aaf810b6755736.gif[/img]

[h3]Here you can find an overview of the most important key data of the expeditions:[/h3]

[h3][b]This is what scouts do:[/b][/h3][list]
[*]Process water and food into rations
[*]Running to ruins to spot them
[*]Scouts can not become explorers to avoid problems and misunderstandings
[*]Scouts bring Explorer equipment to the Expedition Station
[/list]

[h3][b]Explorers are sent on an expedition:[/b][/h3][list]
[*]Need rations (1 for Resource Ruin | 2 for Story Ruin)
-> Required rations = number of Explorer * Action Points
[*]Per ration there is 1 Action Point
[*]Each action point allows you to perform an action
[*]Explorer can be any settler who is not currently assigned as a Scout
[*]Explorers will not be available as settlers during an expedition.
[*]Explorers have only a limited inventory
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/39bda6d3e9442127de34fff60bd6be0f16a59cae.gif[/img]

[h3][b]Resource expeditions:[/b][/h3][list]
[*]Max. 6 settlers can be chosen
[*]No Advantages are available
[*]No equipment can be chosen
[*]No rations are available
[/list]

[h3][b]Story Expeditions:[/b][/h3][list]
[*]Max. 6 settlers can be chosen
[*]Advantages are available
[*]Equipment must be chosen
[/list]

[h3][b]Procedure:[/b][/h3][list]
[*]Build expedition post
[*]Assign scouts
[*]Send out scouts
[*]Exploring the ruin - Scout returns
[*]Scouts prepare rations
[*]Scouts bring Explorer equipment to the expedition post
[*]Explorers gather at the expedition post and equip all resources
[*]As soon as all explorers are on site, they start the expedition
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/fd25eedbbf971b4eef6890f6a8fc26944a6a5b5e.gif[/img]
[*]Once arrived at the ruins, the player is faced with various decision options, each of which mostly costs 1 action point
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/74aba0658e02af171888d98d72890d6768982621.gif[/img]
[*]If the action points are empty, the expedition must return.
[*]If all possibilities are exhausted, the expedition must return.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/80b7455e92a811a010b23e0dfd5b2cef3409b2ba.gif[/img]
[*]The player can transfer found resources into the inventory of the settlers and must pay attention to the capacity.
[*]Expedition returns home and gathers again at the expedition post
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/538ed226d04f8237c06c32b3dc33bb396c617c94.gif[/img]
[*]Resources are stored in the expedition post and then distributed by settlers in the settlement.
[/list]


[h2]Expeditions Feature Trailer[/h2]
[previewyoutube=FMfYed_3wiU;full][/previewyoutube]

We know that there are a few more things we need to address and we are listening to your feedback. We're trying to address all the important issues in a timely manner and make the game as a whole more understandable and fair. notes.title: Patch #002 - Early Access - Fixes & Balancing
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/7771e08823c11fca9dde9a473e9c50b8feb01d58.png[/img]

[b]Hey there survivors![/b]

With the last patch we have adapted the settlers and their behaviour regarding hunger and thirst. This made it easier for players to deal with an emergency situation and to juggle with low resources.
Nevertheless, there seemed to be considerable problems to get out of an emergency situation and to bring heavy bursts of food and water back to a good level. In this patch we have focused on the consumption of settlers and adjusted a few things so that it is now easier to recover.

We have summarized the most important points for you and would like to explain why many questions and inconsistencies have arisen. Many players have noted. that they need to assign over 50% of their settlers just to gather water and food and still did not manage to provide enough for all settlers. Clearly this was not intended and we tackled this issue first. So, what was going wrong?

[h2]Water and food consumption was too high and players could not recover after droughts or falling below a certain threshold[/h2][list][*][b][i]After we tried to improve the consumption of settlers overall, we noticed, that this is probably not enough. Once your settlement fell in one or both resources to 0, settler aimed on fulfilling their need for hunger and thirst so fast, that a player could simply not get out of the low resource levels. Basically settlers produced not enough to start a stockpile, but just immediately satisfied their hunger and thirst. Now, water carriers can collect more water in one sweep and plants collected in the forest yield more food. We also adjusted the behaviour of settlers even more, so being able to recover from droughts is now easier.[/i][/b]
[/list]

[h2]The Cultivated Fields were covered, even though there was no Weather Station build[/h2]
[list][*][b][i]We had an issue, where starting a new game would load up certain states of the Savegame before. For this reason Fields and Rain Collectors could have been covered[/i][/b]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/eeaf459ebeb01edf2f143de20507ffaba9b2d2a0.gif[/img]
[list]
[*][b]Cisterns[/b] and [b]Water Towers[/b] will now correctly register [b]Jettys[/b], [b]Wells[/b] and [b]Rain Collectors[/b] that are farther away.
[*][b]Dirt Roads[/b] will now correctly increase settler movement speed when loading a [b]Savegame[/b].
[*][b]Weather Station[/b] settings are now correctly reset when loading a [b]Savegame[/b] or starting a new game.
[*]The [b]Irrigation Plant[/b] no longer radiates the surroundings when irrigation is set to “None”, has no water in inventory or is paused.
[*][b]Irrigation Plants[/b] and [b]Rain Collectors[/b] now display the [b]High Radiation World Icon[/b] if their water is medium or highly radiated.
[*]Zooming with the Keyboard now works as intended using the default or numpad  - and + buttons.
[*]The second message when a mission was finished or failed no longer displays with a random delay.
[*]The intro video now respects the audio volume, set in the options menu (bound to master volume).
[*]Buildings now update their resources within their area of influence correctly in the UI.
[*]Fixed different wrong tooltips.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/9b45befc9d99249c0c5d7ab04bd584eb3146e462.gif[/img]
[list]
[*][b]Fishers[/b] are working faster.
[*]All [b]Seeds[/b] on the [b]Cultivated Field[/b] grow faster now.
[*]Enforced the game to continue in the background when tabbing out of the game window.
[*][b]Water Carriers[/b] get more water in one sweep (before: [b]20[/b], now: [b]25[/b]).
[*][b]Berries[/b] and [b]Mushrooms[/b] yield more food.
[*]Tweaked the hunger and thirst behaviour of settlers to make it possible to recover from extreme food/water shortages.
[*]The water amount stored in [b]Rain Collectors[/b] and Wells is now taken into account in the global resource UI at the top of the screen.
[*]The game now starts in the monitor's native resolution instead of Full HD, when starting the game for the first time. This prevents the misconception that higher resolutions are not supported. Please note: Running the game in 1440p and above is currently not optimized.
[*]Changed the distribution of some ruins so it doesn’t look as artificial as before and make other ruins pop out more.
[*]Changed the position of tooltips on decrease production limit buttons from top to bottom in the Building UI.
[*]Increased default Production Limit for Water to 90,000 and for Food to 5,000.
[*]The water and food shortage check, which trigger the red warning in the Resource UI on top of the screen, now take the amount a children needs to eat and drink into account (previously every settler was calculated as adult, even children).
[*]Toggling through buildings or settlers now selects them and opens their inspector UI.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/ec24c6b5efe3d99ce3ed2c8ca69509be7727a983.gif[/img]
[list]
[*]The Forester Lodge and its work mode: “Cut & Reforest” is currently unbalanced. Trees are cut down faster than the time it takes to replant and regrow them.
[*]The irrigation plant currently adds radiation, instead of only leveling radiation to the current radiation level of its inventory.
[*]Settlers currently do not get the protection clothing with the best protection value but simply the one that is the closest.
[/list]

[h3]We know that there are a few more things we need to address and we are listening to your feedback. We're trying to address all the important issues in a timely manner and make the game as a whole more understandable and fair. However, it is important to remember that Endzone - A World Apart is a survival game, so we have made it challenging with full intention.[/h3]


- Your Team from Gentlymad & Assemble Entertainment

notes.title: Patch #001 - Early Access - Fixes & Balancing
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/602a11bf2d6b0a360427bb16a20a86508eda316e.gif[/img]

Hey there survivors!

We had several reports from players in Steam, on our Discord and even on Reddit about balancing issues. We investigated your feedback carefully and knew we had to find a solution for this.

we have summarized the most important points for you and would like to explain why many questions and inconsistencies have arisen. Many players have noted. they are not having enough water or food available. Most of the time this problem happened either at the beginning of a new round or after a drought, so we have modified several systems.

[h3]Settlers now survive longer without food or water[/h3]
[list]
[*][b][i]we implemented this in order to make it easier for the player to recover from situations where no food or water is left. This often caused the settlement to completely fall apart.
Now it should be easier to recover from dire straits.[/i][/b]
[/list]

[h3]Cultivated fields and orchards wither away much slower during a drought[/h3]
[list]
[*][b][i]Crops on cultivated fields and orchards withered away completely during a drought.
This often caused an entire harvest to be lost and created a very hard setup for the future of your settlement. Your crops had to regrow entirely from scratch and produced no food for the next couple of seasons. 
Now all crops only lose some of their food amount during a drought, setting the food production back but not destroying it outright.[/i][/b]
[/list]

[h3]We fixed a bug concerning settler homes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b][i]It was sometimes the case that settlers would not search for homes, even though there were homes available. This has been fixed.
We also improved when and how settlers look for a home. If a settler dies and was living in a house, homeless settlers and settlers that are living in shelters will now try to move into that house. The same is done when a house is upgraded.[/i][/b]
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/eeaf459ebeb01edf2f143de20507ffaba9b2d2a0.gif[/img]
[list]
[*]Fixed a Bug were settlers wouldn’t move into empty houses
[*]Inhabitant Amount of buildings should no longer exceed
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/9b45befc9d99249c0c5d7ab04bd584eb3146e462.gif[/img]
[list]
[*]Tweaked Hunger and Thirst values of Settlers to be less punishing
[*]Tweaked the impact of droughts on the environment to give the player better chances to survive after a drought
[*]Children now spend more time in school per visit
[*]Inventories of buildings and the Resources in the HUD on the upper edge of the Screen now give more feedback regarding amounts of resources that are reserved to be picked-up by settlers for consumption or work tasks.
[*]Improved “No Resources” tooltip of Market
[*]The Profession List in the Profession Menu now also outputs the settlers, that will take over the respective profession soon.
[*]Camera Zoom has been tweaked and now has additional zoom levels
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/ec24c6b5efe3d99ce3ed2c8ca69509be7727a983.gif[/img]
[list]
[*]When the patch is played using a Savegame of an earlier version, the reserved amount for food might currently show a negative number.
[/list]
[h3]We know that there are a few more things we need to address and we are listening to your feedback. We're trying to address all the important issues in a timely manner and make the game as a whole more understandable and fair. However, it is important to remember that Endzone - A World Apart is a survival game, so we have made it challenging with full intention.[/h3]

Have a great sunday and a good start into the next week!

- Your Team from Gentlymad & Assemble Entertainment

notes.title: Community FAQ & Known Issues
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We have checked and answered a lot of your reviews and feedback you to the game. Most of the points are often similar in content and are slowly drawing a pattern by which we can identify and already address the problems. We know that many of you are frustrated with the game for various reasons, as many things are either not explained sufficiently or simply need to be optimized in balancing.
For this reason, in this thread we will list the most frequently asked questions of the community and try to give a general answer or explanation.

[h1] Please note that we are already addressing and evaluating all known problems.[/h1] 

[list]
[*]Why do Water Carriers do not use water that is stored in Rain Collectors?
[*]Settlers prefer the Jetty and the Well over the Rain Collector. They do this to give the Rain Collectors time to fill up and be full if the lake dries up during a drought.
[/list]

[list]
[*]Why do settlers die even if enough water/food is available?
[*]Settlers have to walk to the Watertower/storage to get water and food. If those buildings are too far away, the settler might die of thirst/starvation while trying to reach the source.
[/list]

[list]
[*]Why do children not move into a free house?
[*]Children only move into houses if their parents live there as well.
[*][b]Note that we are aware of a current bug of people not moving into houses or shelters anyway![/b]
[/list]

[list]
[*]Why do we need a Refinery when Recyclers do the same job?
[*]The Refinery works much faster than the Recycler and stands as an upgrade to the building. It's size and construction costs are a hinderance though when placing it in your settlement. Recyclers can be used to craft resources very close to the building (e.g. the tailors shop or the workshop) that need those resources.
[/list]

[list]
[*]Why are my people sad even though i have a Graveyard?
[*]The Gravekeeper/Mortician needs to collect the corpses in order to remove them form from your settlement. Ss long as they remain uncollected the debuff appears.
[/list]

[list]
[*]The repair function is bugged or builders do not want to repair stuff!
[*]After a sandstorm nearly all of your buildings are damaged. A builder has to collect the resources needed for the repairing and bring those to the building. If your settlement consists of dozens of buildings (which it often does at that time) your builder will take quite long to do so. The more builders you have the faster your buildings will be repaired.
[/list]


[list]
[*]Why is "Build next" not doing exact that?
[*]Builders will only start constructing a building if all resources are brought to the construction site. These resources are brought to the construction site by all your settlers (not just the builders). Since the settlers, that are not builders ignore the "Build Next" button, it might happen that other buildings are constructed first.
[/list]

[list]
[*]After a sandstorm or drought settlers consume more food and water?
[*]Your settlers always consume the same amount of water and food. The problem lies not within the settlers consumption but rather in the water/food production. During a drought all plants wither away. Your fields need to regrow and berries/mushrooms need some time to recover as well. This means that your production is severely cut down, which might be perceived as an increase of food consumption by your settlers.
[*][b]Note that we are aware of that and currently working on this![/b]
[/list]

[list]
[*]Why can I not cover my orchards, but cultivated fields?
[*]We implemented this because the trees planted in orchards are to high to place a cover over them. Orchards produce significantly more food then cultivated fields. In order to balance this we gave the fields the advantage of being able to be covered.
[/list]

[list]
[*]What is the importance of a Market?
[*]The market moves resources out of your storage halls and into the market. Settlers now have a centralized place where they can get their food/water/tools/protective clothing/medicine etc. They have to spend less time wandering around to collect everything they need.
[/list]

[list]
[*]My settlers wont stop producing kids - is there a way to stop this?
[*]There is no stop function right now. As long as there are free cabins your settlers will produce children.The most reliable option right now is to build shelters. Settlers who live in shelters do not produce more offspring.
[/list]

[list]
[*]After 90% of my settlers are dead, I cannot recover. This seems unfair!
[*]This problem often shows itself in conjunction with a shortage of water/food. This usually happens after a drought, when your food and water production suffered a significant hit. During a drought all plants wither away. Your fields need to regrow and berries/mushrooms need some time to recover as well. This means that your production is severely cut down, which can cause your settlers to be unable to produce enough resources to feed themselves.
[/list]

[list]
[*]Settlers die to fast or do not live long enough!
[*]This is correct. We are currently working on making this more balanced and do not punish the player to hard.
[/list]


[h2]We hope this covers a lot of your questions and concerns. We are sorry for the inconvenience and hope you still enjoy the game. We try hard to adapt the game as soon as possible so that the mentioned problems do not occur anymore or appear comprehensible. Thanks for the detailed and extensive feedback![/h2]

Greetings Survivors,

after more than 150 years and many generations in the [b]Endzones[/b], we are finally ready to venture to the surface again. The last 6 weeks in Closed Beta have already shown us some dangers and taught us important lessons. Now it's time to found a new civilization and start a new attempt on the earth's surface in [b]Early Access[/b].

[i][b]We made it, Survivors![/b]
Since the announcement in October, there has been a very fast growth within the fan community. We hope that the Early Access will strengthen this even more. The Closed Beta gave us a deeper insight into your gaming behaviour and showed us early on possible optimizations and frequently mentioned wishes. It was a good opportunity for us to collect feedback and to adjust the further development steps with regard to the upcoming Early Access. We are really happy about the awesome feedback we received from our community that has build itself over the last months. We wish you a lot of fun and encourage you to keep the feedback coming![/i]


[url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/933820/discussions/0/2137462524937411579/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/db129d941f7d67ddee9462723769d76f517552f9.gif[/img][/url]

[b]Savegames[/b]
[list][*]During Early Access we can not guarantee [b]savegames[/b] to work across updates. We will do our best to avoid broken savegames and ensure compatibility, but there will be cases where we will have to make a clean cut and break support for older files.
[*][b]Closed Beta savegames[/b] are no longer compatible with the Early Access release version and can not be loaded from the Main Menu.
[/list]
[b]UI[/b]
[list][*]The [b]Statistics View[/b] is currently very rudimentary and not fully implemented. Enhancing this view as well as giving more insights into the state of your settlement will be part of further updates. The first of this kind is planned as a sidetrack in May.
[*]We translated the game into several [b]languages[/b] right from the start. However, due to the dynamic nature of the game and our fast iteration cycles, some translations may be outdated or wrong. If this is the case we are happy if you could point out any translation issues.
[*]Parts of the [b]User Interface[/b] are subject to change due to user feedback and internal decisions to improve the overall experience.
[/list]
[b]Features[/b]
[list][*]The game currently features a first prototype of our [b]Side Mission[/b] system. This system will be overhauled as one of the first steps during the Early Access. Our target is to better integrate Side Missions into the game flow, to improve concerning feedback and to embed them into small narrative snippets around your settlement with more challenging goals.
[*]At Early Access release the game features all core mechanics in a challenging and intriguing sandbox mode as well as some mid-game features like Electricity. [b]Lategame[/b] content is our main focus and will be enhanced during the further development of the game.
[*][b]Local Expeditions[/b] are part of our first Early Access milestone. However, small fractures of this feature might already be visible in the game and might lead to confusion.
[/list]
[b]Bugs[/b]
[list][*]The logisticians of [b]Markets[/b] currently ignore the restrictions set on the building that limit which resources should be stored in this building.
[*]If the Game Time is paused the [b]Task Completed[/b] window of a finished mission on the bottom of the screen is delayed until the Game Time is unpaused.
[/list]

notes.title: Food Supply in Endzone - A World Apart
notes.content:
[h2]Food Supply through Farming, Hunting, Fishing and Gathering[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/9e1e5bf0cf43ffed7d4f38abedb0e35e14d503fb.gif[/img]

Generally a functioning food supply is elementary for the survival of a civilization. Both in a modernized society and in a primitive community of settlers, balanced and sufficient food is essential for survival.
In [b]Endzone - A World Apart,[/b] a food supply needs to be created in different ways. A varied diet is just as important for the settlers as enough food in general. For this reason, early and elaborate planning of food supply is an important step, which punishes even small mistakes later in the game. A insufficient variety of food can also cause sickness across the settlement due to low nutrition in the overhaul diet of a settler.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/c668c44ca820993c79a5922dffd8315dd70258a4.gif[/img]

[h2]Food Variations:[/h2]
[list][*][h3]Seeds:[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/d9bfb1b020094a8adfc2dd1a3dd3a66c49ce882f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/a8c4635be9d8e14948edd1ebe866f7ae28cc2902.png[/img]

At the beginning of a New Game the player is provided with a small number of different [b]Seeds[/b], which vary on every new map. By creating [b]Fields[/b], these can be planted and grown into crops. At the beginning of the game it is recommended to create at least one [b]Field[/b] with a [b]Seed[/b] and to assign some settlers to the profession [b]Farmer[/b]. As soon as a plant is fully grown, it is harvested by a [b]Farmer[/b] and must be replanted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/be2bfb135a894f5ade9381d06fac03fed349d89b.gif[/img]

A special feature here is the possibility of harvesting not fully grown plants early. Although this reduces the yield, it can prevent the entire harvest from withering in a period of drought. 
In addition, new [b]Seeds[/b] can only be planted once the current crop has been completely harvested.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/39c795143a95cdd817775f37c2ca603ea655b6c3.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/08ae528369ef761264fc8da7f3de933c779359c9.gif[/img]

[i]Possible [b]Seeds[/b] are currently: Corn, Wheat, Hemp, Squash, Cabbage, Beans, Pepper and Potatoes[/i]

[*][h3]Plantations:[/h3]
Besides [b]Seeds[/b] for [b]Fields[/b], Endzone also has seeds for plantations. Various trees that spawn fruits or nuts can be grown on special fields, that differ slightly from the regular [b]Fields[/b]. These trees have an initial growth time which they need in order to yield food. After a [b]Plantation[/b] tree has grown it will yield food every season. Your farmers can harvest food from these trees for several seasons until they have to be replanted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/fa8f86966f6ec73be9b1efd84054b4a757965772.jpg[/img]

[i]Possible [b]Seeds[/b] are currently: Plum, Nut, Cherry, Pear, Pecan, Apple, Peach, Walnut[/i]

[b][i]Important: We are currently planning to enhance [b]Fields[/b] and [b]Plantations[/b] with a drawback. The player needs to vary between different crops between seasons to minimize the possible decrease of the nutrition levels in the ground. Using the same seed over and over again might also cause the outbreak of plagues, making the player actively search for new seeds by sending out Expeditions.[/i][/b]

[*][h3]Meat:[/h3]
Meat can be obtained in two different ways. Firstly, by building a [b]Fishing Hut[/b], the settler can establish a supply of fish as long as the corresponding lake is filled with water. Additionally, by building a [b]Hunting Lodge[/b], the surrounding animal population can be hunted and processed.
[list]
[*][h3]Fishing Hut:[/h3]
As long as a water source is in the immediate vicinity, the [b]Fishing Hut[/b] is usually built at the beginning. Only as long as the lake holds water, fishermen can generate food through fishing. In a drought period, the fish stock succumbs.
Always keep an eye on whether the associated lake holds water or is dried out so that your workers can be transferred to other professions and not waste their time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/eff29ceaf4f3eb3b7fc8cb3364986d4d5a6c5ade.gif[/img]

[b][i]Important: Several Fishing Huts in the immediate vicinity reduce the yield, as they decimate the same fish stock.[/i][/b]

[*][h3]Hunting Lodge:[/h3]
In Endzone - A World Apart, animals roam in herds. The [b]Hunting Lodge[/b], like many other buildings, has an Area of Influence that must be moved depending on the position of the animals. Excessive hunting can completely exterminate a stock and bring the food supply to a standstill.
Always keep an eye on whether the terrestrial wildlife is moving outside the range of the building and adjust the hunting grounds accordingly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/72a5b3bd97c4aef7311daaf5c8ae0c88ee71abe4.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/29e1e609a9deb035c96cabc4a745b6083ea43c50.gif[/img]

[b][i]Important: If hunting is too excessive, whole species can become extinct and therefore, in the long run, bring the food supply to a standstill.[/i][/b]
[/list]

[*][h3]Berries and Mushrooms:[/h3]
The [b]Gatherer Hut[/b] enables settlers to gather berries and mushrooms from the surrounding forests. These berries and mushrooms only grow within a forest biome and, like other plants, wither if the soil is too dry. In case of a drought period, the gatherer often cannot generate food and the production succumbs.
It is advisable to have a constant overview of the humidity in the surroundings. Should no more plants grow, workers can be transferred to other professions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/bd50038d7a4ffd738791f0b6842560727febf131.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/0cd0ce89204a13c92c42f6e9145019b3fd6384e4.png[/img]

[b][i]Important: Just like Fields and Plantations, an [b]Irrigator[/b] can irrigate the surrounding forest and thus positively influence the growth of berries, mushrooms and roots.[/i][/b]

[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/4187c3d3bf6a1c2c0657a1fb77b77d7fdd5f168c.png[/img]

[b]Note[/b]: This is a brief but already quite detailed overview about the food supply in Endzone - A World Apart. The shown processes and dependencies are always under development and might be changed or optimized in future updates.

[i][h2]Thank you for all the great support and immense feedback we are obtaining through you! We are already working on implementing some requested features and improvements.[/h2][/i]

[url=https://discord.gg/HF7SaH7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/a1fb23da4f8837100258611e6cd889668cc9f464.png[/img][/url]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/933820/Endzone__A_World_Apart/

notes.title: Water in Endzone - A World Apart
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/10d9717496531dafdc560a2d64810990db6bdc3b.gif[/img]

[h1]Water supply and systems[/h1]

Water plays an important, if not the most important role in [b]Endzone - A World Apart[/b]. The beginning of a new settlement already puts the player in front of several challenges which often only become apparent a long time later. Even if the water supply seems sufficient at the start, this status does not last long.

A functioning and constant water supply is the cornerstone for the survival of the settlers and is subject to constant control and optimization from beginning to end. Since each map in the Endzone is different from the previous one through its procedurally generated environment, it is always necessary to use various tactics to establish a water supply.

In order to give you an overview of the possibilities, we will introduce you to water and the corresponding systems in Endzone - A World Apart.

[h2]Watertower & Boardwalk[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/65b72decd2d07b7c1d089c6313c314c1b0c4ad38.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/1591a61299377e52e468fb3bc38556ca4176f31c.gif[/img]

As already shown in the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NV1Snd7seUI&t=30s]"How-To-Play"-Trailer[/url], the beginning of a new settlement is immediately initiated with the construction of a [b]Watertower[/b] and a [b]Boardwalk[/b].
Through this simple production chain, water is scooped from the nearby lake and put into the water reservoir. Pay attention to the placement of the Watertower since it is aimed to be near a boardwalk and will only function in the immediate area as well.

[b][i]Important: The water supply will only take place if appropriate "carriers" are assigned to collect water.[/i][/b]

[h2]Well[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/ac023138babcefc844d2fdc6ca3c8566eaebca3f.jpg[/img]

It is not uncommon for a settlement not to be built in the immediate vicinity of a natural water source. In this case the supply via a [b]Watertower[/b] and a [b]Boardwalk [/b]is almost impossible.
For this purpose we have developed the [b]Well[/b]. This building can be used to pump groundwater from the immediate area and distribute it to the next [b]Watertower[/b]. Of course, the yield is significantly lower and the necessary manpower is all the greater.
A [b]Well [/b]therefore only serves as a temporary water supply in an emergency. It is essential for the player to build towards the water source in a timely manner and to expand the water supply. Several wells can be built, but there must be a certain distance between the individual buildings, otherwise they work less efficiently.

[b][i]Important: The Well can also provide a small water supply in periods of drought, even if lakes have dried up and there is no rainfall.[/i][/b]

[h2]Rain Collector[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/8d545cc5bb35d4fed30f642fe2ad862271402e81.jpg[/img]
[i]Rain Collector uncovered and covered from radioactive rain[/i]

A [b]Rain Collector[/b] can also be built at a later date. This building makes it possible to obtain water from precipitation. The water is automatically stored in the [b]Rain Collector[/b]'s tank and even in periods of drought emptied by "carriers" and transported to the [b]Watertower[/b]. Since it can never be said with certainty when and how many periods of drought the environment will catch up with, an extensive water supply through rainfall is essential in the later game. Lakes take too long to be refilled, just as well as wells only create weak water supplies.

[b][i]Important: Contaminated rain, as already described in "Radiation & Humidity", is collected unfiltered by the Rain Collector and used as drinking water in the settlement. Always check whether the rainfall is contaminated and whether the Rain Collector needs to be covered.[/i][/b]

[h2]Irrigation & Fertility[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/b4e8e0cd446731eb7429cab6f4c8797bcfa07f80.png[/img]
[i]Different steps of fertility shown in the regular view[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/28c5359d798e1769094c3fb80dfb1cdaaebe5d38.png[/img]
[i]Different steps of fertility shown in the Water Heatmap[/i]

As in real life, there is no uniform distribution of resources in the environment in Endzone - A world apart. Water, the basis of all life, is also scarce in some areas. To make dry land fertile and usable, there is the possibility of installing irrigation systems. 

In addition to dry soils, forests also benefit from a functioning water supply, as berries, herbs, trees and mushrooms can grow.  It is also important to maintain a balance between making the soil fertile and supplying water to the settlers. 

As can be seen in the pictures, foresighted planning is advantageous, because the fertilization of soils is a resource-intensive process - and certainly no one wants to see his settlers starve when other food sources are exhausted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/59280ba1a46884576b0db4b0d9895ce4907d46d8.gif[/img]

[b][i]Important: Water for the Irrigator is taken from the Watertower. Always keep an eye on your supply, so your settlers won't die of thirst.[/i][/b]

[h2]Charcoal Burner & Filtration[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/5179bbac5fb3fee42af90ea885012927590e1901.gif[/img]

The [b]Charcoal Burner[/b] seems at first glance to have nothing to do with water supply, but it represents an elementary building later in the game. Lakes can be contaminated by toxic rain and [b]Rain Collectors[/b] only collect acidic water through contaminated rainfall.
By coal filtration in the [b]Watertower[/b] the contamination can be reduced. Clean water is essential for the supply in the settlement. Contamination in drinking water can lead to diseases, just as irrigation with radioactive water can lead to contaminated fields.

[b][i]Important: The [b]Charcoal Burner[/b] uses wood to produce coal. Always keep an eye on your supply or you might run out of building resources![/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/9e78e5631dbab9515b9c59bfe9a4b3c0b8d8ce20.jpg[/img]
[i]Watertower without and with a coal filtration system[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/4187c3d3bf6a1c2c0657a1fb77b77d7fdd5f168c.png[/img]

[b]Note:[/b] This is a brief but already quite detailed overview about the water system in Endzone - A World Apart. The shown processes and dependencies are always under development and might be changed or optimized in future updates.

[h3][i]We hope we could provide you with a good overview of the complex systems behind Endzone - A World Apart. We thank you for all the great feedback, support and discussions about our game![/i][/h3]
[url=https://discord.gg/HF7SaH7][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/f827ebe02bf65c8f4acb629be6e8e6cbe8e9e5b6.png[/img][/url]

notes.title: Radiation & Humidity in Endzone - A World Apart
notes.content:
[h1]Realistically simulated environment[/h1]

[b]Endzone - A World Apart[/b] places great emphasis on realistically simulating nature and the environment. Weather effects and radioactive radiation are not only visually present for the atmosphere, but are actually simulated.
Radiation is calculated at the beginning of a map and distributed as a weak threat.
Weather conditions are primarily expressed by the humidity of the soil, but cloud formation and possible rainy areas are also marked.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/9140436d264d86eeec3dd724a8e1829f1cac9b0d.gif[/img]

[h1]Water Heatmap[/h1]
To give the player control, the environment maps can be toggled with two buttons in the UI. The Water Heatmap colors the complete map into humid and arid areas. Cloud formation is also simulated in realtime and can be followed and observed.
It is relevant for the player to check how dry or humid an area is.
Dry areas reduce the growth rate of fields and can bring them to a complete standstill. When completely dry, the crop withers and the fields are destroyed. Manual irrigation is essential and can determine whether or not a drought can be survived.
The environment adapts visually to the humidity and expresses itself by dry or even missing grass up to dry soil and desert-like landscape.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/982959524624735cc6dc52f4e8bef6e2494ad4ea.png[/img]

[i][b]Humid and arid landscape in comparison[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/d9ab7d730af3e23139251b89292840a8960c0a8e.png[/img]

[b]Pro Tipp: cloud formation in most cases leads to rain, which in turn irrigates an area naturally. But beware: it can also be radioactive rain.[/b]

[h1]Radiation Heatmap[/h1]
Radiation is the biggest threat in the Endzone. In the long run, radiation affects the health of settlers and can spread rapidly. Contaminated lakes pose a threat to the nutrition of the inhabitants, as the water is both drunk and used to irrigate the harvest. Radioactive rain can affect the fields and contaminate the food: a protective plastic roof is essential.
Before a new area is developed, settlers remove the soil and the radiation. Without adequate protective clothing, this quickly becomes a disaster. 
The Radiation Heatmap can be used to check whether and to what extent an area is contaminated. Alternatively, the environment offers an indicator through a bluish glitching effect at the edge of the screen. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/a1677f30479cea3be6755d4266115efc843af44f.png[/img]

[i][b]Non contaminated and radioactive are in comparison[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/ba4d79c08e63ad54d8a8a2e40f1c88c3bd917707.png[/img]

[b]Pro Tipp: a large number of flowers grow in particularly contaminated areas.[/b]

[h1]Overview & Map key[/h1]

It is not always directly clear which color stands for which circumstance. For this purpose, players always find a current map key for the respective maps and can orient themselves on it. Be aware that the map key might change in the future and will be a constant WIP as the game develops.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/d142cbc4b8f49d517c153048dd70121718392367.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/3487eb8707055f42209351b7b5a15041aab02434.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/d73e0e496bcaef87463003d3511f546256193d6f.png[/img]

notes.title: "Prosperity", coming Fall 2021
notes.content:
[b]Rise and shine fellow survivors, rise and shine![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36095472/5ddea5ebbaedff085a2b8191a8b1fc1030934c95.jpg[/img]

After 150 years away from the poisonous surface, the last human survivors emerged, ready to take back the planet! Thanks to their relentless determination, things are finally starting to look better, and the people are reaching for: “Prosperity”! 

The expansion will focus on [b]new endgame content and automation to grow bigger settlements[/b]. It will also introduce [b]new materials, buildings, scenarios, and a lot of new, useful technologies[/b].

~~~
[h3]Watch the new Prosperity trailer here:[/h3]
[previewyoutube=63lWXCjj4fM;full]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=63lWXCjj4fM[/previewyoutube]

[h3]Wishlist the Prosperity Expansion on Steam now:[/h3]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1632320/Endzone__A_World_Apart_Prosperity/

[h3]Features of the Prosperity Expansion:[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Live Your Best Life:[/b] With growth and security comes luxury, and hot new items like beer, cake, coffee, and thankfully, soap for survivors to enjoy!
[*] [b]Built to Last:[/b] New construction materials like sand, concrete, metal, and cement will ensure your buildings can withstand the toughest environmental challenges.
[*] [b]Expand Your Industry:[/b] New materials and more spare time means growing the colony’s production capabilities with all new buildings, including sand huts, aqua farms, and concrete factories
[*] [b]New Adventures:[/b] The Prosperity update will introduce three brand-new scenarios that will test the limits of the next generation of survivors.
[/list]

We are awaiting you outside the Endzone, survivors!
